evals.prompt: Every night at 02:00, mark `subscription` records whose `renewal_date` has passed as `lapsed`; `status` is a readonly field only automation may change.
evals.expected_output: A `defineFlow` with `type: 'schedule'`, the cadence on the START NODE's `config.schedule: { type: 'cron', expression: '0 2 * * *' }` (no top-level `schedule`), `runAs: 'system'` (a readonly field is stripped under `runAs: 'user'`); one `update_record` with a where-map `filter` (`renewal_date: { $lt: '{today}' }`) and `fields: { status: 'lapsed' }` (not `values`), `label` on every node, `edges` (never `next`), an `end` node.

evals.prompt: When an opportunity reaches stage `closed_won`, send the account owner an inbox notification with the deal name.
evals.expected_output: A `record_change` flow bound on the `start` node `config`: `objectName: 'opportunity'`, `triggerType: 'record-after-update'`, bare-CEL `condition` `previous.stage != 'closed_won' && record.stage == 'closed_won'`; a `notify` node with `recipients: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.owner_id' }`, `title: 'Won: {{ record.name }}'`, `channels: ['inbox']`; `requires` lists `automation`, `triggers`: `messaging` is always-on, listed only under `--preset minimal` (else notify reports success with `skipped: true`).

evals.prompt: Build an autolaunched flow `crm_budget_approval` on `project`: when `budget` increases past 100000, route to a manager who can approve, reject, or send it back to the submitter for revision; a resubmission returns to the manager. Cap it at two send-backs.
evals.expected_output: The ADR-0044 shape: an `approval` node (`type: 'approval'`, `approvers: [{ type: 'position', value: 'crm_manager' }]`, `lockRecord: true`, `maxRevisions: 2`) with `approve` / `reject` out-edges plus a `revise` out-edge to an `approval_revise` node, and a resubmit edge back into the approval node typed `type: 'back'` — what legalises the cycle for `registerFlow`. The flow lives in `flows` (no `approvals` collection).

evals.prompt: Build a guided 'new client onboarding' wizard: step 1 collects company details, step 2 asks whether a credit check is needed (if yes, a credit-check screen; else skip), then creates the `account` record.
evals.expected_output: The steps BRANCH, so a `screen` flow (`type: 'screen'`), not a form-view wizard: a `screen` node per step, a `decision` whose out-edges carry mutually exclusive `condition` predicates (an unguarded out-edge always runs, in parallel), a `create_record`, explicit `variables` entries (`{ name, type, isInput, isOutput }`), every path reaching an `end`; `runAs: 'user'`.

evals.prompt: Add a step calling our `pricing.recalc` function to compute the discount and save it on the quote, then post the quote to our tax service over HTTP; if the tax call fails, route to a handler node instead of failing the run.
evals.expected_output: A `script` node with `config.function: 'pricing.recalc'` (registered via `defineStack({ functions })`), `inputs` and `outputVariable: 'recalc'` — pure compute, so a following `update_record` persists `fields: { discount: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'recalc.discount' } }`. The `http` node sets `timeoutMs`. Failure routing is a `type: 'fault'` edge; a bare error label routes nothing.

evals.prompt: When a `job_application` is approved, email the applicant — not a user; the address is the record's `applicant_email` field.
evals.expected_output: `notify` with `recipients: { emailField: 'applicant_email' }` (the fourth recipient form: an `email` field of the trigger record) and `channels: 'email'` alone — never a CEL envelope over `record.applicant_email`, which must yield user ids and fails for an address no user holds.

evals.prompt: An expense approval only holders of `expense.approve_request` may start; route to the `crm_finance_manager` position; the submitter must never approve their own expense.
evals.expected_output: Flow-level `requiredPermissions: ['expense.approve_request']`, checked at every door that starts the flow (never a run-user positions check inside it); the `approval` node names `approvers: [{ type: 'position', value: 'crm_finance_manager' }]` with `excludeSubmitter: true`, and `onEmptyApprovers` is anything but `auto_approve`, refused beside it.

evals.prompt: A screen flow: the user uploads the signed contract PDF on the last step; the flow then creates the `contract` record with the file in `signed_copy`.
evals.expected_output: A `type: 'screen'` flow whose last `screen` carries `{ name: 'signed_copy', type: 'file', required: true }` and resumes with the `sys_file` id bound to `signed_copy`; a following `create_record` writes `fields: { signed_copy: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'signed_copy' } }`, claiming the file for the record.

evals.prompt: Build a screen flow `crm_convert_lead` that asks for a company name and a contact name, creates a `crm_account` and a linked `crm_contact`, and ends on a screen linking to both new records.
evals.expected_output: A `type: 'screen'` flow: a `screen` collecting `company_name` and `contact_name`; two `create_record` nodes with `outputVariable` (`account`, `contact`), the contact linked by `account: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'account.id' }`; a last `screen` of two `type: 'record_link'` fields with `reference` (`crm_account`, `crm_contact`) and `defaultValue: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'account.id' }` / `'contact.id'`, no `required`, `placeholder` or `options`. The `end` carries no `message` (refused when completed), the `description` no markdown link — the links are the `record_link` fields, never the object field type.

evals.prompt: The `expense` record page shows Edit to every member who can read the record; while an expense is under approval, non-participants still get the button and their save is refused with `409 RECORD_LOCKED`. Let the page know the record is locked before offering the edit.
evals.expected_output: Read the lock itself: `client.approvals.getRecordLock('expense', recordId)` (`GET /api/v1/approvals/records/expense/:recordId/lock`) answers `{ locked }` to anyone who can read the record — the lock hook's own judgement — so the page hides Edit while `locked` is `true`. Not the request row: a non-participant is served none, and request content stays behind `approvalsVisibleToReaders`. An unreadable record answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, like a missing one.

evals.prompt: When a `contractor` is marked `onboarded`, grant its linked user (`contractor.user_id`) the `crm_contractor_portal` permission set; run the flow as system so the grant always lands.
evals.expected_output: Not as system: a system-context insert into `sys_user_permission_set` (as into `sys_user_position`, `sys_invitation` or `sys_member`) is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` — elevation does not lift a governed identity write, a system subflow included. The flow runs `runAs: 'user'`: its `create_record` on `sys_user_permission_set` is judged by the delegated-administration gate as the user whose write fired it, recorded as `granted_by`; a user the gate would not let grant the set is refused — the rule, not a defect.

evals.prompt: Spread new `crm_case` records evenly across the support team; a `refund_requested` case needs sign-off from the support-leads queue.
evals.expected_output: An assignment rule, not a flow or hook: `defineAssignmentRule({ name: 'crm_case_intake', object: 'crm_case', entries: [{ name: 'all', assignTo: { type: 'queue', value: 'crm_support_team' }, strategy: 'round_robin' }] })` in `assignmentRules` — evaluated once per insert on a still-ownerless row, never on update; no counter field. The sign-off is an `approval` node (`type: 'approval'`) with `approvers: [{ type: 'queue', value: 'crm_support_leads' }]`: the queue's members join the slate at node entry; an empty queue adds nobody.

evals.prompt: HotCRM (`hotcrm`, version 3.2.0) ships the flow `crm_deal_won_alert`. We want it to also create a billing task, with no second copy running beside it. Where does our version live, and how is it switched off if we need to?
evals.expected_output: A flow with the same name `crm_deal_won_alert` in HotCRM's paired package `hotcrm.custom`, its body declaring `overrides: { package: 'hotcrm', basedOn: '3.2.0' }`: it is armed in the base's place (one reload, no window with both bound), keeps the base's name and its one activation switch — `POST /api/v1/automation/crm_deal_won_alert/toggle` with `{ enabled: false }` turns it off for this deployment — and a run suspended on the old body finishes on that body. Not a clone: `POST /api/v1/automation/crm_deal_won_alert/clone` is "new similar", a second flow under a new name that lands switched off in the pair; not an undeclared same-named flow (refused at publish); not an edit of HotCRM's own flow.

evals.prompt: When a `crm_case`'s `priority` becomes `urgent`, send its owner an inbox notification; clicking the notification should open that case.
evals.expected_output: A `record_change` flow bound on the `start` node `config` (`objectName: 'crm_case'`, `triggerType: 'record-after-update'`, condition `previous.priority != 'urgent' && record.priority == 'urgent'`) and a `notify` node with `recipients: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'record.owner_id' }`, an inline `title`, `channels: ['inbox']`, and no `sourceObject` / `sourceId` / `actionUrl`: a notify that writes none of the three links to the run's trigger record, here the case. An explicit pair or `actionUrl` is only for linking elsewhere and wins when written; half a pair is dropped, never defaulted; a run with no trigger record (a schedule tick) links nowhere. `requires` lists `automation`, `triggers` (`messaging` is always-on).

evals.prompt: Email the opportunity owner and the sales manager when an opportunity has sat in one stage for 30 days; the subject must show the `stage` as its label, in each recipient's own language.
evals.expected_output: The notify node names a mail `template` (never inline `title` / `message`, which are one text for every recipient), and the template's subject prints the stage with the mail formatter `{{ stage | option:opportunity.stage }}` — the argument a bare `object.field`, no quotes — so the renderer prints that recipient's label from the field's option list in the recipient's locale. Not `label()` in `templateData`: the map is evaluated once per run, before recipients fan out, so it cannot differ per recipient; and `option` is mail-only, refused in an inline `title` / `message`. The stage value itself reaches the template as stored (`stage` in `templateData`).

evals.prompt: When a saved `deal` record's `status` is changed to `submitted`, route it to the sales manager for approval, and tell the person who clicked Save "Sent {{ record.name }} to your manager for approval" on the save toast, in their own language.
evals.expected_output: A flow whose start node binds `objectName: 'deal'` with `triggerType: 'record-after-update'` and the condition `previous.status != 'submitted' && record.status == 'submitted'` (on update `previous` is bound), then a `save_notice` node (`config.message: 'Sent {{ record.name }} to your manager for approval'`) placed BEFORE the approval node (`type: 'approval'`): the run is still inside the write there, while a `save_notice` reachable after the approval (or a `wait`) is refused at parse. The translation lives under `flows.<flow>.notices.<node_id>.message`, read in the saver's locale. Not a `notify` node to the saver (an inbox message, not the save answer), not a page banner component (shown whenever the record's state says so, not for this save), and not in a subflow the trigger flow calls (a child run holds no save, so the node refuses by name).
